needs_review: AUTH KEPT AS SCAFFOLDED, and it matches the vault entry byte for byte: Basic base64(api_key:api_secret). services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js key 'fivetran' (line 4219) collects api_key and api_secret and its testHeaders builds `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${creds.api_key}:${creds.api_secret}`).toString('base64')}` against testEndpoint https://api.fivetran.com/v1/users, which is exactly what auth {type: basic, userField api_key, passField api_secret} plus test GET /v1/users sends. No new vault field was needed and none was invented.

SHAPE-PROOF RESULT (real run, 2026-09-12, 1 iteration): verbatim overall line 'fivetran  SHAPE_PROVEN  proven=5 authwall=0 ambiguous=0 failed=0 inconclusive=0 skipped=0'. The differential is strong here because Fivetran routes BEFORE it authenticates: the control probe at the bogus path https://api.fivetran.com/quox-shapeproof-control-b35a1639 answered 404 with {"code":"NotFound","message":"HTTP 404 Not Found"}, while the test call and all four tool paths answered 401 with {"code":"AuthFailed","message":"Invalid authorization credentials"}. Different status AND different error code at the real paths, so host, TLS, base_url, the Basic auth header and every path below are proven. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: no Fivetran credential was held, so a 2xx has never been observed on this connector and no response body has ever been seen. Beta at best, never Stable on this evidence.

RESPONSE PICKS ARE DOCUMENTARY, NOT OBSERVED. Every Fivetran v1 response is wrapped in {"code":"Success","data":{...}}, so the picks are data-prefixed and list picks read data.items[] with next_cursor from data.nextCursor; 'code' is surfaced deliberately so a non-Success envelope is visible to the caller rather than silently shaped away. The field sets come from the REST API reference, not from a 2xx we have seen, so a pick may be over- or under-selective (most likely on list_destinations, where region, time_zone_offset and setup_status are the fields the docs describe).

list_destinations uses the account-wide GET /v1/destinations. The 401-versus-404 differential above is what makes that path claim real rather than a guess: a route Fivetran does not know answers 404 NotFound on this host, and /v1/destinations answered 401 AuthFailed like every other live path. Per-group destination detail (GET /v1/destinations/{destination_id}) is not modelled.

READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: all four tools are GETs and none is marked write:true. Fivetran's mutating surface is deliberately unmodelled, including POST/PATCH/DELETE on /v1/connectors, /v1/groups and /v1/destinations, connector schema changes (PATCH /v1/connectors/{id}/schemas) and the sync triggers POST /v1/connectors/{id}/sync and /resync. Adding any of those needs write:true and the write-path review, not a draft edit.

PAGINATION IS CURSOR-BASED AND MANUAL. limit is clamped to a default of 20 and a maximum of 100 (the API itself allows up to 1000); the caller pages by feeding next_cursor back into the cursor input. Spec v1 has no auto-pagination, so a large account is only ever seen one page at a time.
